chain.g: mute, dumb, silent, unable to speak, inarticulate

ety.text: From Middle English muet, from Anglo-Norman muet, moet, Middle French muet, from mu (“dumb, mute”) + -et, remodelled after Latin mūtus.
From Middle French muetir, probably a shortened form of esmeutir, ultimately from Proto-Germanic.
From Latin mutare (“to change”).

senses.d: Not having the power of speech; dumb.
Silent; not making a sound.
ex: He ask’d, but all the Heav’nly Quire ſtood mute, / And ſilence was in Heav’n: […]

senses.d: Not uttered; unpronounced; silent; also, produced by complete closure of the mouth organs which interrupt the passage of breath; said of certain letters.
Not giving a ringing sound when struck; said of a metal.
A stopped consonant; a stop.
An actor who does not speak; a mime performer.
ex: As for the poor honest Maid, whom all the Story is built upon, and who ought to be one of the principal Actors in the Play, she is commonly a Mute in it:

senses.d: A person who does not have the power of speech.
ex: The girl left, and presently returned, followed by two male mutes, to whom the Queen made another sign.

senses.d: A hired mourner at a funeral; an undertaker's assistant.
ex: He asked about the undertaking business, and how many mutes went down with Lady Estrich’s remains […]
Then followed a long silence during which the mute turned to them and said, ‘Of course you'll be wanting an urn, sir?’

senses.d: An object for dulling the sound of an instrument, especially a brass instrument, or damper for pianoforte; a sordine.
An electronic switch or control that mutes the sound.
A mute swan.
An action of muting, especially in a discussion forum as a penalty for breaking rules.
To silence, to make quiet.
To turn off the sound of.
ex: Please mute the music while I make a call.

senses.d: To cause the content or messages of (a social media account, a website, etc.) to no longer appear on one's feed, trigger notifications, or similar, especially without fully blocking.
Of a bird: to defecate.
ex: I Mute as a hauke dothe whan ſhe hath endued her gorge.
And I knewe not that there were Sparrowes in the wall, and mine eyes being open, the Sparrowes muted warme doung into mine eyes, […]

senses.d: The faeces of a hawk or falcon.
ex:
On which was written not in words,
But hieroglyphic mute of birds

senses.d: To cast off; to moult.
ex: Have I muted all my feathers?

grp.label: not having the power of speech

senses.d: Having the same relationship, each to each other.
ex: They were mutual enemies.

senses.d: Collective, done or held in common.
ex: Mutual insurance.

senses.d: Reciprocal.
ex: They had mutual fear of each other.

senses.d: Possessed in common.
ex: They had been introduced by a mutual friend.
On his area the pursuer built a dwelling-house, of which the gable and garden-wall were mutual with his neighbour Smith […]

senses.d: Owned by the members.
A mutual fund.
A mutual organization.

senses.d: That which has mutated, with one or more new characteristics from a mutation.
Someone or something that seems strange, abnormal, or bizarre.
ex: Your neighbor seems to be a mutant; he’s so cringy!
She could really get to like this relationship with Raven, if it weren't for the fact that he's a homicidal mutant.

senses.d: Synonym of mutex.
A changed version of a program, developed as part of mutation testing.
Of, relating to, undergoing (i.e. mutating), or resulting from change or mutation; that has undergone mutation.
ex: mutant DNA
Scientists have created a mutant enzyme that breaks down plastic drinks bottles—by accident.

senses.d: Strange, abnormal, or bizarre.

senses.d: Any alteration or change.
Any heritable change of the base-pair sequence of genetic material.
A mutant.
An alteration in a particular sound of a word, especially the initial consonant, which is triggered by the word's morphological or syntactic context and not by its phonological context.
The transfer of title of an asset in a register.
A group of thrushes.
ex: Birdwatchers would enjoy a host of sparrows, a herd of swans, a descent of woodpeckers, a herd of wrens, and mutation of thrushes.
Names for a group: A flute or mutation of thrushes.
